question: There have been reports since 2021 that the Italian customs administration and the Guardia di Finanza have been seizing private aircraft registered in non‑EU countries that are permanently based in the European Union.

The Italian authorities are basing these seizures on national customs legislation (Article 36(4), Presidential Decree No 43/1973), which states that transferring an aircraft’s registration to a non-EU country causes it to lose its EU goods status, resulting in a new import duty obligation once the six‑month temporary importation period has elapsed.

On the grounds of smuggling, which is categorised as a continuing offence, these aircraft are being seized after being hangared in the EU for decades without complaint. A proof of customs clearance dating from the time of import offers no protection. This practice bases the loss of status purely on national registration status, even when the aircraft never physically leaves the customs territory of the EU.
This can create friction with the Union Customs Code as laid down in Regulation (EU) No 952/2013, as well as with the primacy of EU law. 1.

Does the Commission share the view that EU goods which have been duly released for free circulation should only lose this status if they are actually removed from the customs territory, and not because their registration has merely been transferred to a non-EU country while they remain within the customs territory?
Is the Commission aware of this practice, and if so, what is its position on the matter?
Is the Commission planning to consider measures to address this?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (16.9.2026) According to Article 153(1) Union Customs Code1, all goods in the customs territory of the EU are presumed to have the customs status of EU goods, unless it is established that they are not EU goods. Ιn principle, means of transport located in the EU or released for free circulation therein are deemed to be EU goods.

The flag, plate or any other means of registration of the means of transport is irrelevant to determine the customs status of means of transport. The establishment of a non-EU status of the goods can only be assessed effectively by the competent national authorities, based on the information and documentation available to them.

To this respect, the processes and conditions for a change from an EU registration of a means of transport to a non-EU registration, which are established by other-than-customs legislation, may affect the assessment on the customs status of the means of transport.

If the non-EU status of an aircraft is established, while it is in the EU, then the aircraft must be placed under a customs procedure in the EU or be re-exported. Unless the aircraft is released for free circulation in the EU, the temporary admission procedure is the procedure allowing the (non-EU) aircraft to be used in the EU, under certain conditions.

The Commission is not aware of any relevant national practices in Italy breaching the provisions of the Union Customs Code. Regarding the seizures of the private aircrafts, the establishment of such measures, their scope and conditions are decided at national level.
